To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we calculate the inclusive $J/psi$ production via initial state photon radiation and gluon radiation at NLO in the perturbative QCD, and the results are consistent with the Belle measurement.

the QCD N$^2$LO calculation of $e^+\ e^-$ to $J/\psi + X$ is consistent with the experimental results of Belle and much smaller than the experimental results of BESIII in low CM energy range, which indicates that the perturbative expansion is not convergent in this region and the QCD mechanism for $J/\psi+X$ production at low energy should include the contributions from the non-perturbative region.

the perturbative expansion of QCD on $J/\ψ$ production via initial state radiations becomes worse as the center-of-mas energy of $e^+$ $e^-$ collider becomes lower and closer the $J/\psi +X +\gamma$ production threshold.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the inclusive $J/ψ$ production at ${{e^ +e^-}}$ colliders.
the perturbative QCD predictions of $J/\psi $ inclusive production in the $e^+ e^-$ annihilation.
the QCD perturbativeness of $J/\psi+X$ production in $e^+ e^-$ collisions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the QCD perturbations on $J/\ψ$ inclusive production via initial-state radiation are consistent with the Belle and BESIII measurements at high CM energies.
the convergence of perturbative QCD expansion on $J/\Psi$ production becomes worse as the center-of-masses energy becomes lower and close to the inclusive $ J/\Psi $ production threshold.

the QCD prediction on inclusive $J/\Psi$ production at ${{e^{\pm}}}{{e}^{\pm}}$ collider with the center-of mass energy range from 2.5 to 10.58 GeV is consistent with the Belle experiment data at 10.58 and 10.52 GeV, but much smaller than the BES III experiment data at lower energy range.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the QCD perturbatively calculated $J/\psi+X$ production cross section at the CM energy range 3.7--10.6 GeVs is consistent with the Belle and BESIII measurements.
, the QCD NLLA prediction is consistent with the Belle experiment at 10.6GeV, but it is much smaller than the BESIII measurement at low CM energies.
the NLO QCD calculation is reliable for the inclusive $J/ψ$ production at the CM energy above 10.6GeV and the initial state radiation is important for $J/\psi $ production.
The main takeaway from our work is that
perturbative predictions for $J/\psi $ production at low energy is not reliable, and the initial state radiation process should be considered.
the QCD perturbatively calculated cross sections are much lower than the experimental data at low CM energy and close to the threshold of inclusive $J/\Psi$ production.
the QCD prediction for $J/\psi +X$, $e^+ e^- \to J/\psi X$, at the BESIII energy range is much smaller than the measured value, and the QCD NLL prediction is still smaller than the measurement.
